checks: A positive-volume compact convex anchor has a positive maximum-volume inscribed simplex. After mapping its ordered vertices to 0 and the coordinate vectors, every coordinate has absolute value at most one by replacing the corresponding simplex vertex. Choosing the orientation before the map and dilating by the inverse d-th root of its absolute determinant gives determinant +1 and radius at most √d(d!a)^(1/d).

A section of B normal to x has supremal essential area at least b/(2R). The pyramid over any section has height at least T−R and lies in L. Integration gives V≥b(T−R)/(2dR), including d=1 with counting measure for a nonempty point section.

A bounded source gives a translated scaled copy in the target with volume at least λ_*^d v and radius at most λ_u D. A bounded target controls each source by its inverse coefficient. Since 0<λ_*≤1, these two bounds compose within the asserted factor on one hyperedge, and there are at most |P_i|−1 expansions. For a singleton only the anchor bound is needed.

For any representation supported on the limiting positive sites, a source with fixed λ>0 supplies |K_z|≥λ^d|K_u|. This persists after division by each positive total mass and passage to the limit. The trivial representation already has its target in the support.

Checked the original notes 2a5bf571e6159901 §§1–2 and dbf3b23d25004153 §3, (3)–(5), including both archived candidate digests. The finite-volume radius and propagation formulas match the source. The normalized support claim has no uniform volume-floor hypothesis.

dependencies.mapping: Apply to the fixed finite base. Its minimal-face hyperedges are exactly the target and all positively weighted other sites in the chosen representation, so connectivity gives the finite expansion order and makes λ_* well-defined for a nonsingleton.
